data.question: Does 'review triage' without --gate apply to critic regardless of where the finding lives?

data.body: Finding numbers are per gate. Omitted --gate: refuse (exit 1) naming the gates that have findings when several do; resolve and name the gate when exactly one does; explicit --gate unchanged. CLI and MCP; MCP description byte-neutral.
data.title: review triage without --gate is refused or resolved, never defaulted to critic (fixes bug Bca71987363)

chunk_findings.detail:
The resolution only treats a gate as "having findings" when *every* entry in its `chunk_findings` has a `digest`:

```python
withf = sorted(
    g for g, r in it.gates.items()
    if (r.evidence or {}).get("chunk_findings")
    and all(f.get("digest") for f in r.evidence["chunk_findings"])
)
```

Gates that have findings but contain at least one undigested entry are silently dropped. That such findings exist is confirmed by this same function: immediately below, an explicitly supplied gate is refused when `not all(f.get("digest") for f in found)`, i.e. the code is written to expect undigested entries.

Concrete failure: an item whose `it.gates` contains `critic` with `chunk_findings = [{"digest": "a"}]` and `security` with `chunk_findings = [{"digest": "b"}, {}]`. Run `ddflow review triage ITEM --finding 1 --confirmed --probe "..."` with no `--gate`. `security` is filtered out, `withf == ["critic"]`, so `len(withf) == 1`, `gate` is set to `"critic"`, and a verdict is recorded against `critic` finding 1 — even though two gates have findings and the user may have meant `security`. The stated intent is that this must refuse (exit 1) naming both gates; instead the finding number is applied to the wrong gate, which is precisely the class of bug Bca71987363 is meant to eliminate. The same filter also makes the single-gate case fall through to `gate = "critic"` (a gate that may have no findings) and refuse with a misleading message when the only gate that has findings contains an undigested entry.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:229 (the `withf` comprehension in `triage`)

chunk_findings.detail: The `gate` property description is changed from `"critic (default) or rubber_duck."` (32 bytes) to `"Omit if one gate has findings."` (30 bytes), yet the stated change contract for this fix is that the MCP description be byte-neutral (`CLI and MCP; MCP description byte-neutral`). The functional fix only requires the lambda default to change (`gate=a.get("gate") or "critic"` → `gate=a.get("gate") or ""`); the description edit is unrelated to that fix and alters the bytes of the MCP tool schema. Any consumer or test that pins the MCP tool listing/schema bytes (e.g. a golden `tools/list` snapshot or a description hash) now observes a different payload and fails, because the JSON-RPC `tools/list` output for `ddflow_review_triage` includes each property's description verbatim. Concretely, a pinned assertion of `... "gate": {"type": "string", "description": "critic (default) or rubber_duck." ...}` (or a hash over it) no longer matches, even though the default-resolution behavior was fixed correctly by the lambda change alone.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:2108

chunk_findings.detail:
The contract stated in the intent and README is: with `--gate` omitted, `review triage` refuses (exit 1) and names the gates that have findings whenever *more than one* gate has findings; it resolves only when *exactly one* does. The implementation, however, counts a gate as "having findings" only when `(r.evidence or {}).get("chunk_findings")` is non-empty **and** `all(f.get("digest") for f in ...)` is true. The digest filter is not part of the stated rule, and a digest-less finding is a real possibility (the very next block has a `not all(f.get("digest") ...)` guard for exactly that shape).

Concrete input: an item whose `gates` are
- `security`: `evidence["chunk_findings"] = [{"digest": "a1", ...}]`
- `critic`: `evidence["chunk_findings"] = [{"digest": "", ...}]` (a recorded finding with no digest)

Running `ddflow review triage <id> --finding 1 --refuted --probe "..."` with no `--gate` gives `withf == ["security"]`, so `len(withf) == 1` and the code **resolves** the gate to `security` and proceeds to append a `review.triaged` event for `security` finding 1. Per the spec ("refused naming the gates that have findings when several do") it should have refused with a message naming both `security` and `critic`, so that the user is told there are findings on two gates and that finding numbers are per gate. Instead the command silently succeeds against whichever gate happens to have complete digests, and the user is never told the second gate has findings — the one case the change was written to prevent. Fix: compute `withf` from gates that merely have non-empty `chunk_findings` (for the refusal/message), and apply the digest check only after a gate has been selected (as the existing `found`/`all(digest)` guard already does).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py (the `if not gate:` / `withf` block, ~lines 228-240)

chunk_findings.detail: The stated intent requires the MCP description change to be byte-neutral, but it is not: the old string `"critic (default) or rubber_duck."` is 32 bytes and the new string `"Omit if one gate has findings."` is 30 bytes. The change edits the serialized tool schema by -2 bytes with no compensating edit anywhere in the surface, so anything that pins the MCP tools blob by byte length (a golden/snapshot of the tool list, or a token/byte-budget assertion over the serialized schema) now differs from the pre-change value that the intent says should be preserved. This is a concrete, mechanical violation of the change's own stated invariant, not a wording preference. (The new text also describes only the resolve case and is silent on the refuse case — omitting `gate` when two gates have findings is now an error — which is exactly the behavior the tool surfaces to the model, but the byte delta is the objectively checkable defect.)
